key_insight: Object placement in indoor scenes can be modeled primarily by local pairwise spatial relations rather than global distributions; learning and composing these local relations (Pair2Scene) yields scalable, precise procedural scene generation. This reduces reliance on large-scale global priors or LLM/VLM reasoning for spatial precision.
problem_solved: Generates high-fidelity 3D indoor scenes despite data scarcity and complex spatial relations, enabling scaling to denser scenes and more accurate spatial arrangements than methods that rely on global distributions or LLM/VLMs.
method: Learn a compact representation of pairwise local object relations (relative position, orientation, contact/occlusion cues) from scene data.
Compose scenes by iteratively assembling objects using the learned pairwise relation primitives, prioritizing local consistency over global distribution modeling.
Use a lightweight relational module (e.g., pair encoders + composition policy) to enable efficient sampling and generalization beyond the training distribution.
impact: Provides a practical, data-efficient route to generate realistic, densely populated indoor scenes for simulation, UI/AR content, and robotics testing—improving spatial accuracy and generalization without heavy reliance on LLMs or massive datasets.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pairwise relation encoder → composition module → final 3D scene

paper_title: Pair2Scene: Learning Local Object Relations for Procedural Scene Generation
paper_authors: Xingjian Ran, Shujie Zhang, Weipeng Zhong, Li Luo, Bo Dai
